coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No employer registration or reporting duty found. Employment Act 2000 and the single national minimum wage apply to domestic workers, but enforcement is weak and the sector is private and informal (searcwl.ac.zw Domestic-workers-Malawi.pdf; africarrieres.com guide). Nothing to build on.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Second-hand and Scrap Metal Dealers Act Cap 50:06 (malawilii.org/akn/mw/act/1971/7) requires dealer registration with premises descriptions. Registering authority, record-keeping duties and fees were unconfirmed because the old.malawilii.org fetch returned 503 and the malawilii.org fetch returned 403. Candidate C8 logged as unverified.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Covered by the same Cap 50:06 Act as scrap dealers (see category 2). No pawnbroker-specific regime found.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Mines and Minerals Act 2023 (Law 25/2023). A mwnation article reports unlicensed foreign buyers and smuggling, and a claim that gold must be sold via the Department of Mines and RBM. No dealer-licence text or register found. Candidate C9 logged as unverified.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No search spent; budget used on categories with clearer regulator signals. Nothing found incidentally.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K08 (livestock movement permits, rejected). No search spent.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Meat and Meat Products Act Cap 67:02 allows slaughter only at licensed or designated abattoirs, and meat marketing regulations (1986) give inspectors access to butcheries. A mwnation report says only 5 designated slaughterhouses exist (2 in Blantyre, 3 in Lilongwe) and inspection is sporadic. Council by-laws license meat premises. Low volume of regulated entities, weak digital fit.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: MBS honey standard MS 366 and voluntary MBS certification. A 2010 source says Malawi was not on the EU third-country honey list because no Residue Monitoring Plan had been submitted, and I could not confirm whether this has changed. No mandatory register or periodic report found.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: A 2024 Frontiers/ILRI study reports fragmented, overlapping regulation between DAHLD and PMRA, untrained vet-shop attendants and a mushrooming of vet drug stores. A Board of Veterinary Surgery registers practitioners. I found no drug-shop licensing or return duty. Candidate C6 logged as unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water Resources Regulations 2018 (GN 11) require a drilling permit, a borehole completion report and an abstraction licence, and drillers need an NWRA certificate. NWRA ran a nationwide declaration drive for illegal boreholes with a 24 Nov 2023 deadline, and Blantyre Water Board and NWRA moved to seal 162 commercial boreholes. Candidate C3 logged.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: UN-Habitat reports private-operator licensing guidelines under the 2016 waste and sanitation regulation, and council by-laws (Lilongwe). Private haulers are few and mostly serve industry. No national periodic return found. Nothing worth a candidate.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: OSHW Act Cap 55:07 has a register of workplaces (s6), steam boiler provisions (ss42-45), a hoists and lifts section (s38), and a six-monthly escalator examination with a report to the Director within 14 days. I could not confirm pressure-vessel rules or any digital system. Candidate C5 logged.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water User Associations run kiosks and rural piped schemes under water boards; the kiosk operator pays the water board from its takings. I found no licence, return or regulator reporting duty (MERA role unconfirmed). Candidate C10 logged as weak.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pesticides Act Cap 35:03 requires a Pesticides Control Board licence to sell or store pesticides. A 2016/17 notice set fees of MK100,000 for wholesale and MK30,000 for retail. In June 2024 CAMA petitioned Parliament over unlicensed traders and PCB non-enforcement. Candidate C4 logged. Fertiliser dealer rules not found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Labour Export Guidelines (2016) require prior Ministry of Labour clearance, and the Ministry warns of prosecution under the Trafficking in Persons Act 2015. Draft Labour Migration Regulations were validated, with enactment unconfirmed. The Israel recruitment arrangement flipped between government-only and private agencies. Candidate C2 logged.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Lilongwe (2018) and Blantyre (2020) City Council cemetery by-laws cover public and private cemeteries, burial permits and grave reservations. No national funeral-home licence or burial-society regulation found. Candidate C7 logged as weak.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: NGO Act 2022 and NGORA require annual licence renewal, annual reports and (from Jan 2025) annual financial audits. On 7 Nov 2024 NGORA reported 344 NGOs without valid licences, 173 without registration certificates and 419 missing 2024 reports; the 31 Dec 2024 and 31 Mar 2025 deadlines were backed by suspension and banking restrictions. Fines were raised to K5m. Candidate C1 logged. No halal or kosher supervision regime found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: The Minibus Owners Association of Malawi (general secretary Coaxley Kamange) is concerned about expired licences and Certificates of Fitness during Maltis outages. DRTSS is moving to e-ticketing and suspends vehicles and licences in Maltis for unpaid tickets. Kabaza is covered by K03. Candidate C11 logged (minibus owners).

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Council market fees (K100/day in Blantyre and Lilongwe, older data) and business licences. Councils collect fees, so there is no duty to a separate authority and no willingness to pay. RBM introduced a new forex bureau licensing framework aligned with the Foreign Exchange Act 2025: shorter licence cycles, higher capital, spot-only trading and mandatory RBM monitoring integration (allafrica 2026-06-26). Candidate C12 logged.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: ECD centres are registered under council by-laws (e.g. Zomba ECD by-laws 2018: register, licence, inspection) and the Ministry of Gender trains and accredits caregivers. There are about 10,000 community-based childcare centres, mostly community-owned. Candidate C13 logged as weak. Driving schools, food producers and hunting outfitters were not searched.

candidates.name: Pharmacy and medicine store licence retention and compliance (PMRA)
candidates.trigger: PMRA Act 9 of 2019; retention fees with surcharge on late payment (Fees and Forms Regulations 2022; amendments effective 1 April 2026).

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: About 200 service stations (MERA, 2018 article). MERA licenses under the Liquid Fuels and Gas (Production and Supply) Act 2004, runs inspections and sets spacing rules (1 km radius). A High Court order stopped MERA's 2017 retail-outlet regulations; whether it was lifted is unconfirmed. No recurring small-operator filing found, and the buyer group is small. Logged as an unverified candidate.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Agricultural Produce (Marketing) Regulations (GN 63/1987, amended GN 14/2008): annual buyer licence renewed before harvest, Malawi nationals only, separate export licence under the Control of Goods Act; 109 traders arrested by May 2021. ACE holds a commodity exchange licence from the Registrar of Financial Institutions, and the warehouse receipt law status is conflicting. Paper licensing with low software value. Logged as weak.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Financial Cooperatives Act 2011 (Cap 46:10) plus the 2013 SACCO Reporting Requirements Directive: monthly, quarterly and annual call returns certified by CEO and finance manager, with fixed late penalties (annual return K20,000 plus K5,000 per day). SACCOs must have an MIS that produces timely returns. Small SACCO supervision is delegated to MUSCCO. An RBM/World Bank single SACCO portal was reported (undated, status unknown). Strongest lead in this pass.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Over 1,000 private facilities are registered with the Medical Council of Malawi. Insurers (MASM, Liberty, Metropolitan, Horizon and others) hold more than 80% of the market and report 25-40% bogus claims. Generic HMS (AfyaPro, OpenClinic, Odoo) exists. No insurer-specific claim format or Malawi vendor found. Logged as weak.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: PMRA Act 9 of 2019 with licence retention fees and a surcharge for late payment (Fees and Forms Regulations 2022; amendment effective 1 April 2026 per ClinRegs, scope unclear). Same buyer and duty as K04; nothing new beyond K04.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No dedicated private security Act or Labour Ministry licensing found. The Justice Minister is reportedly moving to regulate private security firms (uniform and firearm issues). Consolidated Businesses Licensing Act is the general licence. Unverified, thin.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: NCIC registration is mandatory under the National Construction Industry Act (s.20(1)) and renewed annually (licence year ends 31 March). Renewal needs a registration certificate, MRA tax clearance, a MERA permit for electrical contractors, a professional board renewal for consultants, a form and payment; only compliant firms may renew. New Classes 7 and 8 from 3 May 2024; 2024 foreign-contractor regulation requires a joint venture or subcontract with a Malawian firm. Mining local-content rules not found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: The Financial Crimes Act 2017 applies; the FIA ran DNFBP compliance-officer training in July 2023 and is the default supervisor where none is designated (2018 page). ESAAMLG follow-up report dated April 2024. No registration or periodic reporting rule specific to estate agents or lawyers confirmed. Unverified.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
coverage.found: Tourism Act 2025 (Bill 20 of 2025, assented 2 July 2025) replaces the 1968 Tourism and Hotels Act, creates the Malawi Tourism Authority and a registration and licensing framework for enterprises, establishments and practitioners. The old regime had annual licences, a 1% revenue tourism levy remitted to the ministry, defaulter lists and closure campaigns (2023). Transition rules, MTA start date and the levy under the new Act are unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules
coverage.found: Timber: raw round-wood export ban never lifted, timber export licences revoked, MAIWD export permit then Ministry of Trade licence for unprocessed timber and agricultural commodities (WTO profile, undated). Fish and charcoal rules not found. Tobacco already covered by K05. Nothing actionable found.

coverage.category: 31. Gaming, betting and lotteries (MAGLA)
coverage.found: Gaming and Lotteries Act 2022 created MAGLA. A June to July 2026 licence round for sports betting and land-based casinos has closed. Only about 12 operators and 4 casinos are licensed. A 12.5% gross revenue tax (2019 figure) is levied. Operators are few and large; weak.

coverage.category: 32. Mining: small-scale and artisanal miners and gemstone dealers
coverage.found: Mines and Minerals Act 2023 (Law 25/2023). The 2024 Annual Economic Report says licence holders must declare production but artisanal and small-scale miners lack the literacy and know-how, and enforcement is hard. An Artisanal and Small-scale Miners Act was in progress (2023). Licence and dealer licence details were not found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 33. Pension Act 2023 employer remittance
coverage.found: Pension Act 6 of 2023 (effective 1 April 2023): employer 10% and employee at least 5%, remitted by the 14th of each month, penalties and interest, up to K150m. RBM is the supervisor. Arrears K31.1bn and 894 defaulting employers (24.1%) as of an unspecified June. Enforcement reported as weak. Related to K02.

coverage.category: 34. Small food processors: MBS certification and environmental approvals
coverage.found: MBS certification is renewed every two years, with a 50% SME fee subsidy; retailers require the MBS seal. EIA applies per List A/B under the Environment Management Act (one source says it was repealed; unconfirmed). Low frequency; weak.

coverage.category: 35. Data Protection Act 2024 (MACRA registration)
coverage.found: Controllers or processors handling data on more than 10,000 data subjects or data of significance must register with MACRA; some firms get a 24-month grace period from 3 June 2024 (inferred, unconfirmed). MACRA was still consulting on registration fees (notice dated 2026-07). The threshold excludes quiet small businesses; weak.

coverage.category: 36. General business licensing (Consolidated Businesses Licensing Act, Cap 46:01)
coverage.found: Only seen in search results (tradebarriers.org listing and one search summary). It is the general licence regime, with sector licences layered on top. No specific recurring workflow checked; nothing further.
